notes: Custody mechanic data (doc 23 §5.2): pool fees, exchange hack/collapse loss shares, wallet-loss base rate + backup effect. Real names only for sourced factual events; invented names used in events.json for the player's own exchange/vendor unless the event is one of these scripted real ones.

pools.real_basis: Slush's Pool (originally 'Bitcoin Pooled Mining'), announced 27 Nov 2010 on BitcoinTalk

2010.source: early pools often ran fee-free to attract miners; ≈

2011.source: Slush Pool's documented fee is 'around 2%' per Bitcoin Wiki, though the source doesn't pin the year it started — used as a flat estimate 2011-2016

2013.note: GHash.IO ran 0% fees in this era as a deliberate growth strategy (sourced: ViaBTC retrospective) and briefly exceeded 50% of network hashrate 12-13 Jun 2014 as a result — see events_prologue.json ghash_51pct

payout_methods.PPS: Pay Per Share: the pool pays a fixed amount for every valid share you submit, whether or not the pool actually finds a block. The pool carries the variance and charges a higher fee for it.
payout_methods.PPLNS: Pay Per Last N Shares: when the pool finds a block, the reward is split among the last N shares submitted, weighted by who contributed. The miner carries more variance; pools can charge lower or zero fees. Became the more common large-pool model through 2013-14 as pools competed on price — direction sourced (fee pressure), exact adoption year is an estimate.

exchange_events.name: Mt Gox
exchange_events.magnitude: A compromised Mt Gox account was used to crash the displayed price to $0.01 in minutes; Mt Gox rolled back the fraudulent trades and moved 424,242 BTC from cold storage to prove solvency.

loss_share_of_exchange_balance.source: trades were rolled back — real depositor loss from THIS specific incident was near zero, unlike the 2014 collapse

exchange_events.design_effect: A scare, not a loss: trading halts for the rest of the week (no selling), small Heat/household_patience hit, no coin loss. Sets up the 2014 event as the real one to fear.

exchange_events.name: Mt Gox
exchange_events.magnitude: ~850,000 BTC reported missing (~750,000 customer-owned, ~100,000 company-owned); 199,999.99 BTC later found in an old-format cold wallet (20 Mar 2014), leaving ~650,000 BTC unaccounted for.

loss_share_of_exchange_balance.source: derived: ~750,000 of an implied ~940,000 customer BTC on the exchange going effectively unrecoverable for years; game value rounded for playability

exchange_events.repayment_note: Real Mt Gox trustee repayments to creditors did not begin until 2023-2024, a decade later — too far outside the prologue's window to matter; treat as 'gone' for game purposes.
exchange_events.design_effect: Coins on an exchange at this event lose ~80% of their value permanently (game rounding of the real ~80-90% of customer BTC never returned within any relevant timeframe). This is the prologue's central custody lesson.

exchange_events.name: Bitfinex
exchange_events.magnitude: 119,756 BTC stolen (~$72M at the time); bitcoin's market price fell ~20% on the news.

loss_share_of_exchange_balance.source: commonly repeated figure (~36% of Bitfinex's BTC holdings) but NOT independently confirmed by primary sourcing in this research pass — flagged as uncertain

exchange_events.design_effect: A late-game random-chance exchange hack (not scripted to every playthrough): if the player has coins on an exchange in 2016Q3, a small chance (≈10-15%, tune in sim) of losing ~35% of that exchange balance.

base_annual_chance.source: derived from Chainalysis 2017 estimate that 2.78-3.79M BTC (~17-23% of then-circulating supply) were lost forever over Bitcoin's history to date (2009-2017); spread across ~8 prologue years and weighted toward the CPU/GPU/FPGA era when drives were swapped and wallets re-installed more often, ~3%/year is a reasonable game rate

cost_cash.source: backing up a wallet.dat file cost nothing but attention in this era

chance_multiplier_with_backup.source: ≈ a backed-up wallet is only vulnerable to a lost/destroyed backup too, not a single point of failure — cuts the base chance by ~85%

backup_action.duration: lasts until the player changes machines/moves house, per doc 23 §5.2, at which point it should be prompted again

wallet_loss.source: Chainalysis 2017 study (reported via Yahoo Finance, NewsBTC, PaymentsNext, Nov 2017)
